name: Izumi Super Toughness KAI Narrow chain
spec_notes: seamless bushings support precision rollers for a smooth, quiet ride
description:
Specifically designed for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and NJS certified for Japanese Keirin racing, this chain features a very slick, highly-functional PTFE treatment on the plates, bushings and rollers.
This reduces resistance and drag by 10% compared to the traditional Model V Super Toughness when used in combination with top quality chainrings, cogs and a high-performance lubricant, while also increasing hardness, durability and corrosion resistance.

name: Miche Pistard chain
description:
Heat-treated steel construction with a long-wearing chrome plated finish makes the Miche Pistard chain an extremely solid choice, whether for everyday street use or tearing up the velodrome.
Manufactured in Japan by Izumi for Miche, so you know it's good.
ⓘ  Pistard translates to "track cyclist" or "track racer" in English, referring to a cyclist who competes in velodrome events. The term is used in several languages, including French, Italian, and Dutch. There, you learned something today!

name: Izumi 410TG Tough Guard chain
description:
Made in of durable cro-mo steel in Japan, the Izumi Tough Guard is an extra durable choice for all single speed & fixed gear applications that can withstand all kinds of weather and still look nice.
While other "rust busting" chains have a dull finish and look like they are coated with salt, the Izumi Tough Guard uses a trivalent chromium plating to prevent it from rusting and also keep it shiny.

name: Izumi Model V Super Toughness chain
spec_notes: full bushings support precision rollers for a smooth, quiet ride
description:
Made from pure Japanese chromoly steel, this is THE track chain.
One of the few chains that meet the strict certification requirements of the Japanese Keirin Association (NJS), the Izumi-V is renowned among Keirin racers and track riders for its strength and efficient power transfer.
A special high-carbon alloy is used to produce the pins, often used in low-friction ball bearings, which offers a 300% increase in durability compared to a standard chain.
